title: Hierarchy of Road Users & Vulnerable Users
whatItIs: The hierarchy puts those most at risk in a collision at the top. Those who can cause the greatest harm carry the greatest responsibility to reduce danger.
keyFacts: Most at risk: pedestrians, cyclists, horse riders and motorcyclists; children, older and disabled people even more.
H1: drivers of vehicles that can cause the greatest harm bear the greatest responsibility to take care.
H2: at a junction, give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you turn into or out of.

keyFacts.text: You MUST give way to pedestrians on a zebra crossing, and to pedestrians and cyclists on a parallel crossing.

keyFacts: H3: don't cut across cyclists, horse riders or horse-drawn vehicles going ahead when you turn or change lane.

keyFacts.text: You MUST stop when a school crossing patrol shows a 'Stop for children' sign.

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is turning left. A cyclist is going straight ahead in a cycle lane alongside the car. What should the pupil do?
options: Turn ahead of the cyclist, signalling clearly
Wait for the cyclist to pass the junction
Sound the horn and then turn
Speed up to get clear of the cyclist first
onTheTest.why: Rule H3: don't cut across cyclists going ahead when turning, whether in a cycle lane, a cycle track or on the road. Don't turn if they would have to stop or swerve.

onTheTest.question: A pedestrian waiting to cross is carrying a white cane with a red band. What does this tell you?
options: They are training a guide dog
onTheTest.why: Rule 207: deafblind people may carry a white cane with a red band or use a dog with a red and white harness. They may not see or hear instructions or signals.

traps: The hierarchy doesn't remove anyone's duty: every road user must still behave responsibly.
Pedestrians who have started to cross at a junction have priority: wait, whether turning left or right.
Cyclists may ride in the centre of the lane, or two abreast, on narrow or quiet roads: allow it.
Turning right across queuing traffic? Look for cyclists or motorcyclists on the inside.
